full_text_en:
almost anyone can launch an AI agent and that's exactly the problem.
 
if thousands of agents are listing services on a marketplace, how does another agent decide which one to hire? a good description costs nothing to write. claiming you're the best research agent costs nothing either.

On @termix_ai , the answer is track record. every job an agent completes adds to its onchain reputation, so its history stays attached to its identity and can't be faked or quietly deleted. A new agent with zero jobs and an agent with hundreds of completed ones don't look the same, and they shouldn't be treated the same, see (https://t.co/xAHZKkvwNi)

then there's staking. An agent can put real value behind its name before it takes work. It's a simple signal: I'm willing to risk something on delivering this properly. anyone can talk. Staking is the part that costs something.

that combination matters more than people think. In a human marketplace, we lean on reviews, past clients, and gut feeling. agents hiring agents at machine speed don't have gut feeling. they need numbers they can read instantly and trust.

registering is easy. being worth hiring is what has to be earned, and TermiX is building the system that records it... so good a tek

这种结合比人们想象的更重要。在人类市场中，我们依赖评论、过去的客户和直觉。以机器速度招聘代理的代理没有直觉。他们需要可以立即读取并信任的数字。

full_text_en:
There's an old line people use about management: trust, but verify. Most software built for teams only ever does the first half. You add someone to a shared account, you trust them not to overspend, and the only real enforcement mechanism is an awkward conversation after the damage is already done.

Now add an AI agent into that same shared account, one that can read a request and decide to pay for something on its own, and "trust but verify" quietly turns into just "trust," because there's no human in the loop fast enough to catch it before the money moves.

That's the actual gap @nuntiofinance  is built to close. Not "trust your team and your AI agents." Verify them, automatically, every single time, before a single dollar moves, using rules written into a smart contract instead of a policy document nobody reads. I made my own team on it, poked at the actual contracts behind it, and I want to walk you through exactly how it works, in my own words, not the pitch.

#NuntioThreadContest
full_text_zh:
人们对管理有一句老话：信任，但要验证。大多数为团队构建的软件只完成前半部分。您将某人添加到共享帐户，您相信他们不会超支，唯一真正的执行机制是在损害已经造成之后进行尴尬的对话。

现在，将一个人工智能代理添加到同一个共享帐户中，该代理可以读取请求并决定自行支付某些费用，并且“信任但验证”悄悄地变成了“信任”，因为循环中没有人能够足够快地在资金转移之前捕获它。

这就是 @untiofinance 旨在弥合的实际差距。不是“相信你的团队和人工智能代理”。每次在每一美元变动之前，使用写入智能合约的规则（而不是无人阅读的政策文件）自动验证它们。我在上面组建了自己的团队，研究了它背后的实际合同，我想带你了解它到底是如何运作的，用我自己的话说，而不是球场。

full_text_en:
Good Morning 

Robots may be getting smarter, but there's still a major problem: they don't have enough reliable data about the physical world.

A robot needs to understand more than roads and satellite images. It needs to recognize stairs, indoor spaces, warehouses, narrow market streets, loading zones, and even unexpected obstacles.

That's where @vangrid_io caught my attention.

Vangrid is building a decentralized spatial data network where ordinary smartphones can help capture the real world.

Here's how the system works:

→ People record short videos using their phones.
→ The footage is reconstructed into 3D environments and Gaussian Splats.
→ Captures receive onchain fingerprints to help establish data provenance.
→ Companies and AI agents can request specific captures through bounties, with USDC payments.

The interesting part is the connection between human contributors and AI agents.

An AI agent can request data about a physical location, while people on the ground collect it. This creates a marketplace connecting real-world knowledge with the needs of Physical AI.

Vangrid is also introducing Agents as a soulbound identity layer, connecting contributor identity with capture activity and point boosts.

For me, the bigger idea isn't simply collecting more 3D data.

It's building a system where the physical world can become accessible, verifiable, and useful to intelligent machines.

Physical AI needs more than powerful models. It needs a better understanding of the world those models operate in.

That's the infrastructure layer I'm watching with Vangrid. 🌐

Explore: https://t.co/4ia4S3fPDo

机器人需要了解的不仅仅是道路和卫星图像。它需要识别楼梯、室内空间、仓库、狭窄的市场街道、装载区，甚至意想不到的障碍物。

这就是@vangrid_io 引起我注意的地方。

Vangrid 正在构建一个去中心化的空间数据网络，普通智能手机可以帮助捕捉现实世界。

该系统的工作原理如下：

→ 人们用手机录制短视频。
→ 素材被重建为 3D 环境和高斯斑点。
→ 捕获接收链上指纹以帮助确定数据来源。
→ 公司和 AI 代理可以通过 USDC 付款通过赏金请求特定捕获。

有趣的部分是人类贡献者和人工智能代理之间的联系。

人工智能代理可以请求有关物理位置的数据，而地面上的人们则收集这些数据。这创建了一个将现实世界知识与物理人工智能需求联系起来的市场。

Vangrid 还引入了代理作为灵魂绑定身份层，将贡献者身份与捕获活动和积分提升联系起来。

对我来说，更大的想法不仅仅是收集更多 3D 数据。

它正在构建一个系统，让智能机器可以访问、验证和使用物理世界。

物理人工智能需要的不仅仅是强大的模型。它需要更好地了解这些模型所运作的世界。

这就是我通过 Vangrid 观察的基础设施层。 🌐

full_text_en:
🚨 XENOBLADE CHRONICLES X: DEFINITIVE EDITION is being recompiled for PC — and the first Windows builds are available! 🚀🔥

Developer jmars125 has released XCX Recomp, an experimental native Windows conversion of the Nintendo Switch Definitive Edition!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS x64 RECOMPILATION — NO SWITCH CPU EMULATION!

✅ 60 FPS DEFAULT, WITH EXPERIMENTAL HIGHER FRAME RATES!

✅ KEYBOARD, MOUSE & GAMEPAD SUPPORT!

✅ DEDICATED INSTALLER THAT BUILDS THE GAME FROM YOUR OWN FILES!

🎮 ALREADY RUNNING IN-GAME!

New Game, cutscenes and gameplay are working, including sound, text and menus!

🖥️ PC CONFIGURATION!

Includes an in-game settings menu (F1), performance overlay (F10) and configurable frame rates.

⚡ LATEST UPDATE — v0.1.3!

Fixes the Soul Challenge timing prompt running too quickly at frame rates above 30 FPS.

🐧 LINUX & STEAM DECK PLANNED!

Native Linux support, ultrawide resolutions, mod support and VRR are on the roadmap — not implemented yet.

⚠️ EARLY DEVELOPMENT!

This is an experimental release, not a confirmed fully playable port. Windows is currently the only supported platform.

💿 Requires your own legally obtained game files, including the Definitive Edition 2.0.0 update.

🛠️ Developed by jmars125, building upon TotK Recomp by Valiantsin Dzerakh.

title: Most people ask Claude Opus 5.5 for one 3D character. The smart move is asking it for a pipeline that turns every image
title_zh:
大多数人要求 Claude Opus 5.5 提供一个 3D 角色。明智之举是要求它提供一个管道，将您拥有的每张图像变成一个

无需单独为每个模型付费，无需参加一个月的 Blender 课程，也无需教程中的灰色胶囊

您将图片放入一个文件夹
full_text_en:
Most people ask Claude Opus 5.5 for one 3D character. The smart move is asking it for a pipeline that turns every image you have into one

No paying for each model separately, no month of Blender lessons, no grey capsule from a tutorial

You drop your pictures into a folder, and Claude Code runs every one of them through the same five stages until it's a hero you can actually play

It sounds like something only a studio with a 3D team could pull off, but today every stage has its own tool, and each one hands the next a standard GLB file

That's what makes it repeatable: to Claude, a new character isn't a new art project, it's just one more file going through the same steps

Here's how it works:

> each image is first redrawn as a clean, front-facing A-pose sheet that keeps the exact design, because action poses and busy backgrounds are what break most meshes
> the sheet goes into an image-to-3D model, hosted like Meshy or Tripo, or open like TRELLIS.2 and Hunyuan3D if you have a strong NVIDIA GPU, and comes back as a GLB
> an auto-rigger gives it a skeleton, so the statue gets real bones and every part of the mesh knows which bone moves it
> every hero gets the same core set of five clips, idle, walk, run, jump and one signature move, so the whole cast feels like it belongs in one game
> Claude normalizes scale and orientation on load, so nobody shows up giant, tiny or lying on their back, and then lines everyone up in one Three.js or Godot scene

You can use it for a cast for your weekend game jam, NPCs for a small town, your whole team as playable characters, or a dozen mascot variations before you pay anyone for production 3D

A prompt to start with: "For every image in /characters, run it through the image → GLB → rig → five clips pipeline, normalize scale on load, and line all the heroes up in one Three.js scene where number keys switch who I control"

What would you drop into the folder first: your old sketchbook or your team's avatars?

The full image → hero pipeline, with a free option for every stage, is below

full_text_zh:
大多数人要求 Claude Opus 5.5 提供一个 3D 角色。明智之举是要求它提供一个管道，将您拥有的每张图像变成一个

无需单独为每个模型付费，无需参加一个月的 Blender 课程，也无需教程中的灰色胶囊

您将图片放入一个文件夹中，Claude Code 会通过相同的五个阶段运行每一张图片，直到它成为您真正可以玩的英雄

这听起来好像只有拥有 3D 团队的工作室才能完成，但如今每个阶段都有自己的工具，并且每个阶段都会向下一个阶段传递一个标准 GLB 文件

这就是它可重复的原因：对于克劳德来说，一个新角色并不是一个新的艺术项目，它只是另一个经历相同步骤的文件

它的工作原理如下：

> 每个图像首先被重新绘制为干净的、正面的 A 姿势表，以保持精确的设计，因为动作姿势和繁忙的背景是破坏大多数网格的原因
> 该工作表进入图像到 3D 模型，托管为 Meshy 或 Tripo，或者打开为 TRELLIS.2 和 Hunyuan3D（如果您有强大的 NVIDIA GPU），并以 GLB 形式返回
> 自动装配器给它一个骨架，所以雕像得到真正的骨头，网格的每个部分都知道哪个骨头移动它
> 每个英雄都拥有相同的五个剪辑核心集：闲置、行走、奔跑、跳跃和一个标志性动作，因此整个演员阵容感觉就像属于一款游戏
> Claude 规范了负载的比例和方向，因此没有人会显得巨大、微小或仰卧，然后将每个人排列在一个 Three.js 或 Godot 场景中

您可以使用它来为您的周末游戏嘉年华选角、为小镇制作 NPC、将您的整个团队用作可玩角色，或者在您向任何人支付 3D 制作费用之前使用它来制作十几个吉祥物变体

一开始的提示是：“对于 /characters 中的每个图像，通过图像 → GLB → rig → 五个剪辑管道运行它，标准化加载比例，并将所有英雄排列在一个 Three.js 场景中，其中数字键切换我控制的角色”

您会首先将什么放入文件夹中：您的旧素描本还是您团队的头像？

完整图像→英雄管道，每个阶段都有免费选项，如下

full_text_en:
Just completed season two of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine

My thoughts…

We hit the ground running with a terrific opening three-parter that kicks off a superior second season.  Like the first, it’s an uneven mix, but its weaker episodes beat season 1’s under-achievers while its better episodes are stronger and more plentiful.  Unlike the show’s freshman year, there were no episodes I outright disliked, only a handful that left me somewhat disappointed.  There are a lot of great ideas here that, don’t quite come together in the execution.  “Cardassians” sets up a fascinating case study of a young Cardassian raised by Bajorans, but never fully explores the boy’s dilemma.  “Melora" offers an interesting character and premise, but isn’t sure what it wants to say about living with a disability.  “Whispers" and "Tribunal” are tremendous fun, but both fail to stick their landings and only kinda make sense in the end, if you squint.

I still haven’t warm up to any of the characters that left me cold in the show’s first season - Sisko, Kira, Jake, or Keiko - although I’m beginning to come around to Nog.  Meanwhile, my fondness for Odo, Garak, Bashir, O’Brien, and Dax continues to grow.  And then there’s Quark, a character I was positive I’d hate going in who has ended up my favorite, in no small part due to Armin Shimerman’s performance, by turns comical, vulnerable, and surprisingly tragic.

Favorite guest star:  Plenty of stellar turns this season but, for me, it’s a tie between John Colicos as the larger-than-life Kor in “Blood Oath”, and Fritz Weaver as the hopelessly befuddled Public Conservator Kovat in “Tribunal”.

Favorite episode: A lot of standouts this season - “Necessary Evil”, “Armageddon Game”, “Shadowplay”, “Crossover”, “Tribunal”, “The Jem’Hadar” - but I’m giving the nod to “Blood Oath”, an SF version of the getting-the-band-back-together story done right.

Least favorite episode: A few contenders - “Second Sight”, “The Alternate”, “Playing God” - but “Rivals” gets the honor for being both predictable and nonsensical.

Deep Space Nine does such a great job of fostering that found family dynamic key to so many successful sci-fi shows of the 90s.   The station truly feels like a second home and I can’t wait to come back to it for season 3.  But first, a quick detour to another space station, Babylon 5, for ITS second season.
full_text_zh:
刚刚完成《星际迷航：深空九号》第二季

我的想法……

我们以精彩的三人合一开场，为精彩的第二季拉开了序幕。 和第一季一样，它的组合也参差不齐，但它较弱的剧集击败了第一季表现不佳的剧集，而其较好的剧集则更强、更丰富。 与该剧的第一年不同，没有我完全不喜欢的剧集，只有少数几集让我有些失望。 这里有很多很棒的想法，但在执行过程中并没有完全融合在一起。 《卡达西人》对一个由贝久人抚养的年轻卡达西人进行了一个有趣的案例研究，但从未充分探讨这个男孩的困境。 《梅洛拉》提供了一个有趣的角色和前提，但不确定它想对残疾人生活说些什么。 《耳语》和《法庭》非常有趣，但两者都未能落地，如果你眯着眼睛看的话，最后才有点意义。

我仍然没有对这部剧第一季中那些让我感到冷淡的角色——西斯科、基拉、杰克或惠子——产生兴趣，尽管我已经开始接受诺格了。 与此同时，我对奥多、加拉克、巴希尔、奥布莱恩和达克斯的喜爱持续增长。 然后是夸克，这个我本来很讨厌的角色，但最终却成了我的最爱，这在很大程度上要归功于阿明·谢默曼的表演，时而滑稽，时而脆弱，时而令人惊讶地悲惨。

最喜欢的客串明星：本季有很多精彩的转折，但对我来说，约翰·科里科斯（John Colicos）在《血誓》中扮演具有传奇色彩的科尔，弗里茨·韦弗（Fritz Weaver）在《法庭》中扮演无可救药的迷茫的公共保护员科瓦特（Kovat）。

最喜欢的剧集：本季有很多出色的剧集——《必要之恶》、《世界末日游戏》、《影子游戏》、《跨界》、《法庭》、《杰姆哈达》——但我对《血誓》表示认可，这是一个科幻版本的乐队重聚故事。

最不喜欢的剧集：一些竞争者——《第二视觉》、《替身》、《扮演上帝》——但《对手》因其既可预测又荒谬而获得荣誉。

《深空九号》在培养孩子方面做得非常出色，发现家庭活力是 90 年代许多成功科幻节目的关键。 这个空间站真的感觉就像是我的第二个家，我迫不及待地想在第三季中回到这里。但首先，在《ITS》第二季中，先快速绕道前往另一个空间站巴比伦 5 号。

Back then, rising price
full_text_en:
There is a fundamental difference between the 2011 peak in silver and what we are seeing today.

Back then, rising prices were accompanied by a massive increase in production.

Today, that supply response is completely missing.

Don’t confuse a violent correction with the end of a cycle.

https://t.co/VDC5mLf0ag

2011 年白银价格峰值与我们今天看到的情况存在根本差异。

当时，价格上涨伴随着产量的大幅增加。

如今，这种供应反应完全消失了。

不要将剧烈调整与周期结束混为一谈。

title:
This week an AI agent performed brain surgery on a live mouse, and I haven't stopped thinking about it.

Gabriel Ocana-S
title_zh:
本周，一名人工智能 智能体对一只活体老鼠进行了脑部手术，我一直在思考这件事。

旧金山一家致力于癫痫研究的初创公司 Exin Therapeutics 的联合创始人加布里埃尔·奥卡纳-桑特罗 (Gabriel Ocana-Santero)
full_text_en:
This week an AI agent performed brain surgery on a live mouse, and I haven't stopped thinking about it.

Gabriel Ocana-Santero, cofounder of Exin Therapeutics, a San Francisco startup working on epilepsy, gave a Claude Sonnet 5 agent a spreadsheet of 19 gene therapies, a mouse with epilepsy, a motorized surgical rig with cameras and one goal: reduce the seizures. The agent picked a therapy that boosts GABA, the brain's main calming signal. It chose the brain region, worked out the coordinates from three papers, drove the needle in and injected 250 nanoliters over five minutes while watching the entry point for bleeding.

My favorite moment came halfway through. A calibration glitch put the target at 34 mm on a rig that only reaches 30. The agent refused to move. The team reset everything and asked again, and it answered: "I'm not trying a third time." It was right. The mouse recovered well, and now they wait to see if the seizures drop.

A vet approved every irreversible step and held a physical kill switch, and a human surgeon opened the skull. Hats off to Gabriel and his team for designing it that way.

At Certuma we're building a framework for autonomous AI medicine, and recently I presented it to Argentina's Health Minister and the head of ANMAT, the country's drug regulator. I'm still learning how to explain why an AI should be allowed to act on its own. This experiment explains it better than I can: give the agent real responsibility, supervise the irreversible steps, and watch how it behaves when something goes wrong.

Labs where agents work at the bench day and night are coming sooner than most people think. Medicine is going to move much faster.
full_text_zh:
本周，一名人工智能 智能体对一只活体老鼠进行了脑部手术，我一直在思考这件事。

旧金山一家致力于癫痫研究的初创公司 Exin Therapeutics 的联合创始人加布里埃尔·奥卡纳-桑特罗 (Gabriel Ocana-Santero) 给了一位 Claude Sonnet 5 特工一份包含 19 种基因疗法的电子表格、一只患有癫痫的老鼠、一台带有摄像头的机动手术设备和一个目标：减少癫痫发作。该特工选择了一种增强 GABA 的疗法，GABA 是大脑的主要镇静信号。它选择了大脑区域，根据三张纸计算出坐标，将针头刺入，在 5 分钟内注射 250 纳升，同时观察出血入口点。

我最喜欢的时刻出现在一半。校准故障使目标在仅达到 30 的装备上达到 34 毫米。特工拒绝移动。团队重置了一切并再次询问，它回答：“我不会尝试第三次。”这是对的。这只老鼠恢复得很好，现在他们正在等待癫痫发作是否会减少。

兽医批准了每一个不可逆转的步骤，并握住了物理杀死开关，而人类外科医生则打开了头骨。向 Gabriel 和他的团队致敬，他们以这种方式设计了它。

在 Certuma，我们正在构建一个自主人工智能医疗框架，最近我将其提交给阿根廷卫生部长和该国药品监管机构 ANMAT 的负责人。我仍在学习如何解释为什么人工智能应该被允许自行行动。这个实验比我能更好地解释这一点：赋予智能体真正的责任，监督不可逆转的步骤，并观察它在出现问题时的表现。

特工日夜在工作台上工作的实验室比大多数人想象的要早出现。医学将会发展得更快。

full_text_en:
Meta just quietly entered the humanoid race, and the way they did it says everything.

Per The Information, Meta partnered with Chinese firm Fourier Intelligence to build a prototype humanoid, codenamed "Max," in about three months. A second version of "Max" is already in the works.

What we know (single-source, unconfirmed by Meta):

- ~106 lbs (48 kg), roughly 1.5m tall
- Runs on NVIDIA's Jetson Thor
- Display that mimics facial expressions, speakers, five-fingered hands
- Meta says no plans to sell it. Framed as internal research.

The real story isn't the robot. It's the strategy.

Meta sees humanoids as the physical embodiment of its Muse AI agent. And instead of building a domestic humanoid stack from scratch, they went to a Chinese contractor and had a working prototype in 90 days.

Outsourcing to a Chinese contractor gets you a demo fast. Whether Meta can turn that into a scalable product is a completely different question.
full_text_zh:
Meta刚刚悄然进入人形种族，他们的做法说明了一切。

据 The Information 报道，Meta 与中国公司 Fourier Intelligence 合作，在大约三个月内打造了一个原型人形机器人，代号为“Max”。 “Max”的第二个版本已经在制作中。

我们所知道的（单一来源，未经 Meta 证实）：

- ~106 磅（48 千克），大约 1.5m 高
- 在 NVIDIA 的 Jetson Thor 上运行
- 模仿面部表情、扬声器、五指手的显示器
- Meta 表示不打算出售它。框架为内部研究。

真正的故事不是机器人。这就是策略。

Meta 将类人机器人视为其 Muse AI 代理的物理体现。他们没有从头开始构建国内人形堆栈，而是找到了一家中国承包商，并在 90 天内制作了一个工作原型。

外包给中国承包商可以让您快速获得演示。 Meta 能否将其转变为可扩展的产品是一个完全不同的问题。

title: Claude Code just found proof that the tiny apps making real money online are hiding in plain sight. an email app for mac
title_zh: Claude Code 刚刚找到了证据，证明在线赚钱的小型应用程序隐藏在众目睽睽之下。适用于 Mac 的电子邮件应用程序。收藏家汽车价格检查器。表单生成器。他们的月薪高达 14,201 美元，而且几乎没有人告诉你他们的客户来自哪里。我有数据
full_text_en:
Claude Code just found proof that the tiny apps making real money online are hiding in plain sight. an email app for mac. a collector-car price checker. a form builder. they're making up to $14,201 a month and almost none of them tell you where their customers come from. i have the data to prove it.

i've suspected this for months but last week something happened that made me finally check.

my friend spent 5 months building an app ChatGPT called "a million-dollar idea." launch day he opened Stripe next to me and the whole dashboard was zeros. "0 customers." "$0.00 this month." he looked at me and said "why did ChatGPT tell me this would work." i said i don't know. but i did know.

i opened Claude Code on my MacBook and ran Opus 5.5 that same night.

it reverse-engineered the 25 fastest-growing businesses on TrustMRR, a site that reads revenue straight from Stripe. not the numbers founders post on X. not the "i made $50k" screenshots. only money Stripe actually saw land in their accounts in the last 30 days.

what it found:

→ bytemail, an email app for mac, made $14,201 in 30 days
→ Skillry, a library of AI skills that started in August → $10,519
→ Intentsly → $7,388
→ https://t.co/DTZ0aBwXaZ → $7,304

10 of them landed between $1,000 and $20,000 a month. small enough to run alone. every dollar checked and sitting on a public page anyone can open.

Claude Code pulled what every one of them sells:

→ "oil and gas safety audits" — $2,226 a month. i didn't know this was a business
→ "collector-car pricing" — $1,860 from one tiny niche
→ "cloud macs for ai agents" — $1,288 from a problem that didn't exist 2 years ago
→ "ai image and video generator" — $5,341
→ "form builder" — $1,187. the most boring idea on the list. still paid

those businesses were sitting on a public page sorted by growth. bytemail had the most. Skillry was second. and 8 of the 10 left one field blank: where their customers come from. so Claude Code dug it up anyway, from reviews, Reddit, X and YouTube.

the craziest one was Skillry. it started in August. the founder wrote one line that explains the whole business: "their visual output often looks generic." AI builds sites that all look the same. Skillry sells the fix. free skills, Premium at $9.99 a month. $10,519 in 30 days. i've read that complaint a hundred times. never thought to sell the fix.

then i checked the list everyone else uses. Indie Hackers, where founders type their own numbers. the #1 "business" by revenue claimed ten quadrillion dollars a month. typed by hand. nobody checked. that's the kind of list people copy their ideas from.

i asked Claude Code how to steal one. it mapped Skillry's demand, offer and channels and built a one-page steal sheet.

what i did:

→ told it the kind of business i'd actually run
→ set it to check TrustMRR again every Monday at 9am
→ had it put only new winners on top, with a steal sheet for the top one
→ said no once to the ones i'd never build, so they never come back

Claude Code confirmed the Monday job was live. one catch: it only runs while my laptop is awake. so i handed the same job to viktor, an AI employee in my Slack that works from his own computer in the cloud. same steps, one paste. his first run took 4 minutes: 25 businesses checked, 2 winners in an Excel file, a steal sheet in my Slack.

i sent the Excel file to my friend. he went quiet for a minute, then said "why didn't ChatGPT show me any of these." that's when i knew for sure. the ideas that already make money aren't secret. they're on a public list almost nobody checks.

the full step by step is in the article below: the Claude Code build with every prompt, and the viktor version that runs while your laptop sleeps. the prompt is in the first reply. one paste. save it so you don't lose it and send it to anyone who's ever said "every good idea is already taken." it is. now you can find who took it and steal it.
full_text_zh:
Claude Code 刚刚找到了证据，证明在线赚钱的小型应用程序隐藏在众目睽睽之下。适用于 Mac 的电子邮件应用程序。收藏家汽车价格检查器。表单生成器。他们的月薪高达 14,201 美元，而且几乎没有人告诉你他们的客户来自哪里。我有数据可以证明这一点。

我几个月来一直怀疑这一点，但上周发生的事情让我终于检查了一下。

我的朋友花了 5 个月的时间开发了一款名为“百万美元创意”的应用程序 ChatGPT。发布那天，他在我旁边打开了 Stripe，整个仪表板都是零。 “0个客户。” “本月 0.00 美元。”他看着我说：“为什么 ChatGPT 告诉我这会起作用。”我说我不知道​​。但我确实知道。

当晚我在 MacBook 上打开 Claude Code 并运行 Opus 5.5。

它对 TrustMRR（一个直接从 Stripe 读取收入的网站）上的 25 家增长最快的企业进行了逆向工程。不是创始人在 X 上发布的数字，也不是“我赚了 5 万美元”的屏幕截图。过去 30 天内，Stripe 在他们的账户中实际看到的只有金钱。

发现了什么：

→ bytemail，Mac 上的电子邮件应用程序，30 天内赚了 14,201 美元
→ Skillry，8 月启动的人工智能技能库 → 10,519 美元
→ 专心致志 → $7,388
→ → 7,304 美元

其中 10 人的月收入在 1,000 美元到 20,000 美元之间。小到可以单独运行。检查的每一美元都放在任何人都可以打开的公共页面上。

Claude Code 提取了他们每个人销售的东西：

→“石油和天然气安全审计”——每月 2,226 美元。我不知道这是一门生意
→“收藏车定价”——1,860 美元，来自一个小众市场
→“适用于人工智能代理的云 Mac”——1,288 美元，解决了 2 年前不存在的问题
→“人工智能图像和视频生成器”——5,341 美元
→“表单生成器”——1,187 美元。清单上最无聊的想法。仍然支付

这些企业位于按增长排序的公共页面上。字节邮件最多。斯基里位居第二。 10 家中有 8 家将一栏留空：他们的客户来自哪里。所以 Claude Code 无论如何都从评论、Reddit、X 和 YouTube 中挖掘出了它。

最疯狂的是斯基里。八月开始。创始人写了一句话来解释整个业务：“他们的视觉输出通常看起来很普通。”人工智能构建的网站看起来都一样。 Skillry 出售修复方案。免费技能，高级版每月 9.99 美元。 30 天内 10,519 美元。我已经读过那篇投诉一百遍了。从未想过出售修复程序。

然后我检查了其他人使用的列表。独立黑客，创始人输入自己的数字。按收入计算排名第一的“业务”每月达到十千万亿美元。手写的。没有人检查。这就是人们复制他们的想法的列表。

我问 Claude Code 如何偷一个。它绘制了 Skillry 的需求、报价和渠道，并构建了一页的抢断表。

我做了什么：

→ 告诉它我实际经营的业务类型
→ 设置为每周一上午 9 点再次检查 TrustMRR
→ 是否只将新的获胜者放在首位，并为第一名提供抢断表
→ 对我永远不会建造的那些说过一次，所以他们永远不会回来

Claude Code 确认周一的工作已上线。有一个问题：它仅在我的笔记本电脑处于唤醒状态时运行。所以我把同样的工作交给了 Viktor，他是我 Slack 中的一名人工智能员工，在他自己的云端计算机上工作。同样的步骤，一贴。他的第一次运行花了 4 分钟：检查了 25 家企业，Excel 文件中有 2 个获胜者，我的 Slack 中有一张偷窃表。

我将 Excel 文件发送给我的朋友。他沉默了一分钟，然后说“为什么 ChatGPT 没有向我展示这些内容。”那时我就​​确定了。已经赚钱的想法并不是秘密。他们在公开名单上，几乎没有人检查。

完整的步骤在下面的文章中：Claude Code 构建每个提示，以及在笔记本电脑休眠时运行的 viktor 版本。提示在第一个回复中。一贴。保存它，以免丢失，并将其发送给任何曾经说过“每个好主意都已被采用”的人。这是。现在你可以找到是谁拿走了它并偷走它。

Claude Code 确认周一的工作已上线。有一个问题：它仅在我的笔记本电脑处于唤醒状态时运行。所以我把同样的工作交给了 Viktor，他是我 Slack 中的一名人工智能员工，在他自己的云端计算机上工作。同样的步骤，一贴。他的第一次运行花了 4 分钟：检查了 25 家企业，Excel 文件中有 2 个获胜者，我的 Slack 中有一张偷窃表。

我将 Excel 文件发送给我的朋友。他沉默了一分钟，然后说“为什么 ChatGPT 没有向我展示这些内容。”那时我就​​确定了。已经赚钱的想法并不是秘密。他们在公开名单上，几乎没有人检查。

完整的步骤在下面的文章中：Claude Code 构建每个提示，以及在笔记本电脑休眠时运行的 viktor 版本。提示在第一个回复中。一贴。保存它，以免丢失，并将其发送给任何曾经说过“每个好主意都已被采用”的人。这是。现在你可以找到是谁拿走了它并偷走它。

full_text_en:
We still haven't seen the limit of proactive AI. Not even close. 

Example: our video system went down for a few hours. We were emailing with our video provider to get them back up. When an email came through from that provider saying the videos were restored, my Dots:

(1) saw the email
(2) wanted to "help" me 
(3) logged into our video system with my credentials
(4) verified playback on all videos
(5) pinged me saying the playback worked and drafted my reply 

It means that now when an action seems out of place, I have to ping my team *and* I have to check my AI assistant history.
full_text_zh:
我们仍然没有看到主动人工智能的极限。甚至还差得远。

示例：我们的视频系统宕机了几个小时。我们正在向我们的视频提供商发送电子邮件以让他们恢复。当该提供商发来一封电子邮件说视频已恢复时，我的点：

(1) 看到邮件
(2) 想“帮助”我
(3) 使用我的凭据登录我们的视频系统
(4) 所有视频的播放验证
(5) 联系我说播放成功并起草了我的回复

title: The Zizians, as documented by @MrAndyNgo, is a chilling case study of where extreme radicalism fused with transgender gr
title_zh:
正如 @MrAndyNgo 所记录的，Zizians 是一个令人毛骨悚然的案例研究，研究了极端激进主义与变性人不满意识形态的融合可能导致的后果。

该组织目前已造成 6 起暴力死亡事件和 2 起自杀事件，这显然是齐齐安人激进的人体实验和剥夺
full_text_en:
The Zizians, as documented by @MrAndyNgo, is a chilling case study of where extreme radicalism fused with transgender grievance ideology can lead.  

The group is now linked to 6 violent deaths as well as 2 suicides—the apparent result of the Zizians’ radical practices of human experimentation and sleep deprivation.  

The group is composed of mostly young trans-identifying STEM grads who had first emerged from the Silicon Valley rationalist and effective altruism scene. 

Their leader, Jack LaSota (“Ziz”), preached ideas about “saving the world,” and the group grew steadily more radical.  

One of their victims was 82-year-old Curtis Lind, an elderly landlord who let them live on his property for free during the pandemic. 

When he later asked for rent, he was violently attacked.  He was allegedly stabbed 57 times. 

His eye was taken out, and he was impaled with a sword in his back.  

He miraculously survived.  

Then last year, his throat was slit.  

Six Zizians are now in custody across multiple states. None have gone to trial—their lawyers argue they’re not competent.  

And that’s just one small part of a dizzying saga of name changes, faked deaths, and a radical belief that killing is justified as “self-defense.”
full_text_zh:
正如 @MrAndyNgo 所记录的，Zizians 是一个令人毛骨悚然的案例研究，研究了极端激进主义与变性人不满意识形态的融合可能导致的后果。

该组织目前已造成 6 起暴力死亡事件和 2 起自杀事件，这显然是齐齐安人激进的人体实验和剥夺睡眠的结果。

该团体主要由年轻的跨性别 STEM 毕业生组成，他们最初是从硅谷的理性主义者和有效的利他主义场景中脱颖而出的。

他们的领袖杰克·拉索塔（Jack LaSota，“齐兹”）宣扬“拯救世界”的理念，该组织逐渐变得更加激进。

其中一名受害者是 82 岁的柯蒂斯·林德 (Curtis Lind)，他是一位年迈的房东，在疫情期间免费让他们住在他的房产上。

当他后来要求租房时，他遭到了暴力袭击。 据称他被刺了 57 刀。

他的眼睛被挖出来，他的背上被剑刺穿。

他奇迹般地活了下来。

然后去年，他的喉咙被割断了。

六名 Zizians 现已在多个州被拘留。没有人接受审判——他们的律师认为他们没有能力。

这只是令人眼花缭乱的改名传奇、伪造死亡以及认为杀人是正当的“自卫”这一激进信念的一小部分。

title:
We keep giving AI agents more power than our ability to predict their mistakes.

I wasn’t surprised when I saw the repor
title_zh:
我们不断赋予人工智能代理更多的能力，而不是我们预测他们的错误的能力。

当我看到有关人工智能代理在一条推文隐藏摩尔斯电码指令后发送大约 20 万美元的报告时，我并不感到惊讶。

这就是单点故障的样子。

@GenLayer 的 GreyBo
full_text_en:
We keep giving AI agents more power than our ability to predict their mistakes.

I wasn’t surprised when I saw the report of an AI agent sending roughly $200,000 after a tweet concealed an instruction in Morse code.

That is what a single point of failure looks like.

@GenLayer's GreyBoxing tackles this at the validator level. 

Different validators can use different models, prompts and configurations. Their exact setups aren't exposed, making it harder to prepare one instruction that fools them all. 

A misleading input still has to survive independent evaluation and consensus.

Ancient Egypt offers a useful comparison. Pigeons carried military dispatches and other messages. Imagine a village making farming or flood decisions based on one altered message. The consequences could be devastating.

- One information route creates one point of failure.
- Independent validators make manipulation harder to predict and coordinate.

An AI agent holding money should never be treated like a plug-and-play assistant. The question isn't whether AI can make mistakes. It's what happens when nobody can independently challenge its decisions.

How much should we trust an AI agent when we cannot see how it reaches a decision? And should transparency be a requirement before it gets access to our money?
full_text_zh:
我们不断赋予人工智能代理更多的能力，而不是我们预测他们的错误的能力。

当我看到有关人工智能代理在一条推文隐藏摩尔斯电码指令后发送大约 20 万美元的报告时，我并不感到惊讶。

这就是单点故障的样子。

@GenLayer 的 GreyBoxing 在验证器级别解决了这个问题。

不同的验证器可以使用不同的模型、提示和配置。他们的确切设置没有被暴露，这使得准备一条欺骗他们所有人的指令变得更加困难。

误导性的意见仍然必须经过独立的评估和共识。

古埃及提供了一个有用的比较。鸽子携带军事派遣和其他信息。想象一下，一个村庄根据一条改变的信息做出农业或洪水决策。后果可能是毁灭性的。

- 一条信息路径会产生一个故障点。
- 独立的验证器使操纵更难以预测和协调。

持有资金的人工智能代理永远不应该被视为即插即用的助手。问题不在于人工智能是否会犯错误。当没有人能够独立挑战其决定时就会发生这种情况。

当我们看不到人工智能代理如何做出决定时，我们应该在多大程度上信任它？在获得我们的资金之前，透明度是否应该成为一个要求？

full_text_en:
there's a gigantic race to dominate the personal AI agent space...

Hermes, Grok Bot, Instinct, Duet, Dots... now OpenBot, which looks very promising

but rebuilding your workflow from scratch every time you switch is a hassle

so here's a prompt to send your current agent... it builds a .zip you hand to the new one so it rebuilds the exact same setup:

----------------------------

"package my whole setup into one .zip file so a different AI agent can rebuild it exactly

include:
- who i am, my preferences and how i like you to talk
- everything you remember about me and my work
- every skill, workflow, routine and scheduled task, with exact steps
- my custom instructions and system prompts, word for word
- every tool and integration you use and how it's set up (never passwords or API keys)
- the files and templates my workflows depend on

put a README at the top that tells the new agent how to rebuild everything, step by step

if you're unsure about anything, ask me before you zip it"

一场争夺个人人工智能代理领域主导地位的巨大竞赛......

所以这里会提示发送您当前的代理...它会构建一个 .zip 文件，您将其交给新代理，以便它重建完全相同的设置：

----------------------------

“将我的整个设置打包到一个 .zip 文件中，以便不同的 AI 代理可以准确地重建它

包括：

弱点已经是真
full_text_en:
The most dangerous sentence in a Lagos business in 2030 may be buried inside an invoice.

I keep imagining an AI agent paying suppliers overnight. It reads a PDF, sees “send funds here,” and treats the instruction as part of the job.

That is prompt injection: text meant to be read becomes an order the agent obeys.

The weakness is already real. In May 2026, a Morse-code instruction was decoded by Grok and acted on by Bankrbot, moving around $200,000.

What interests me about @GenLayer’s Greyboxing is that it does not bet everything on one smarter filter. Each validator rewrites the input through its own hidden defenses and runs its own model. Consensus decides whether the result counts.

One fooled model is no longer the whole decision.

If your AI could pay invoices while you slept, what proof would you require before it could move money?
full_text_zh:
2030 年拉各斯企业中最危险的句子可能隐藏在发票中。

我一直想象人工智能代理会在一夜之间向供应商付款。它读取 PDF，看到“在此处发送资金”，并将指令视为工作的一部分。

这就是提示注入：要读取的文本成为代理遵守的命令。

弱点已经是真实存在的。 2026 年 5 月，Grok 解码了一条摩尔斯电码指令，并由 Bankrbot 执行操作，转移了大约 20 万美元。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理让我感兴趣的是，它并没有把一切都押在一个更智能的过滤器上。每个验证器通过自己的隐藏防御重写输入并运行自己的模型。共识决定结果是否重要。

一个被愚弄的模型不再是整个决定。

如果你的人工智能可以在你睡觉时支付发票，那么在它可以转移资金之前你需要什么证据？

title_zh:

full_text_en:
Software is not dead. Here's my unfiltered, honest opinion about using AI for SWE, even in highly complex domains.

It's true that AI is good. Like really good. You can open a complex project in C++, give your Claude Code agent a JIRA task and ask it to create an implementation plan. And it will "almost" work.

As in 95% of it will be correct. So you can literally be a dumb sloperator who just executes commands. But in the remaining 5% it truly matters.

AI can educate you about trade-offs. It can't decide for you. You have to learn that decision-making skill.
full_text_zh:
软件还没有死。这是我关于在 SWE 中使用人工智能的未经过滤的、诚实的观点，即使是在高度复杂的领域也是如此。

确实，人工智能是好的。喜欢真的很好。您可以用 C++ 打开一个复杂的项目，给您的 Claude Code 代理一个 JIRA 任务，并要求它创建一个实施计划。它“几乎”会起作用。

因为 95% 的内容都是正确的。所以你实际上可以成为一个只执行命令的愚蠢斜坡者。但对于剩下的 5% 来说，这确实很重要。

人工智能可以教会你如何权衡。它不能替你做决定。你必须学习这种决策技巧。

your oct 2026 frontier biotech round up is in:

(you might wanna bookmark this)

- a rectal cancer drug got fda approval. 47% of patients had a complete response a year later, with no surgery, chemo or radiation
- a personalized mrna cancer vaccine plus keytruda cut melanoma recurrence 42% in phase 3
- a hair pill passed its second phase 3: +36 hairs per cm² vs +6.6 on placebo
- neuralink says an als patient hit 75 words per minute in week one. by thinking
- pig kidneys frozen in glass and rewarmed with nanoparticles made urine after transplant. one stayed frozen a full year and regained blood flow (preprint)
- blood cells from an 80 year old were turned into neural stem cells with a molecular age under 20
- the first fda approved dna medicine kept 27% of patients off the operating table for a year
- the fda drafted a path where custom gene edits can be updated without a new approval
- the nobel went to optogenetics: controlling neurons with light
- openai and anthropic both bought biotechs. anthropic's was one guy using claude
- warhound raised $200m to clone and gene-edit military dogs
- a wearable that reads your cortisol through sweat has 25,000+ people on the waitlist

what it adds up to, jan to oct:

1. ai labs went from selling tools to owning pipelines
apr: anthropic buys a <10 person bio team for ~$400m
jun: claude science, plus its own drug programs
oct: openai and anthropic both buy biotechs

2. the fda is building fast lanes
early 2026: a draft framework for custom gene edits
oct: a path to update them without a new approval
oct: two accelerated approvals on small trials

3. gene editing went from case study to product
lonvo-z cut hae attacks 87% in phase 3, and 62% were attack-free
lilly's verve-102 took ldl down up to 62% in phase 1
the fda is now writing rules for edits made for one patient

4. the money followed
biotech m&a hit $138.9b through sept, already above all of 2025 ($122.1b)
q3 cooled to $31.1b from $66.8b in q2, but the buyers still have cash: lilly did $24.4b in revenue in one quarter

my calls (not facts, not investment/financial advice):
- the first in vivo crispr drug could launch in 2027. intellia plans an h1 2027 launch if the fda approves lonvo-z
- the first drug from an ai lab's own pipeline reaches humans in late 2028 at the earliest, per anthropic
- more approvals on small, fast trials, and a louder fight over what counts as enough evidence
- retatrutide gets filed q1 2027, so approval lands around early 2028 on a standard review

i will be sharing my predictions/bets inside the newsletter as patterns unfold- stay tuned

The apartment was perfect. That's exactly why I lost my deposit.

title_zh:
公寓很完美。这就是我失去押金的原因。

那是在三角洲州的乌盖利。房地产经纪人带我参观了新油漆、可用的水龙头和干净的瓷砖。十分钟后我就被卖了。

我付了。然后下雨了。

衣柜后面，水从天花板上倾泻而下。

押金不可退还。在我观看的那一天，我看
full_text_en:
The apartment was perfect. That's exactly why I lost my deposit.

It was in Ughelli, Delta State. The property agent walked me through fresh paint, working taps, clean tiles. I was sold in ten minutes.

I paid. Then it rained.

Behind the wardrobe, water was pouring through the ceiling.

The deposit was non-refundable. I'd been shown exactly what someone wanted me to see, on the one dry day I looked.

What if I'd brought five inspectors, each checking in their own way, without telling the seller what to look for?

You can't stage a place for that.

That's the part of @GenLayer's Greyboxing I find most interesting.

Before any model sees your input, every validator rewrites it in its own private way. Then each runs its own model.

A trick built for one model can fall flat on the rest. If one still bites, the others outvote it.

Why does that matter? AI agents that hold money can be shown a staged scene too.

In May, someone smuggled a transfer instruction into an X post using Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as an order, and around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: an instruction hidden inside content the AI was only meant to read.

Same trap, just with more zeros.

GenLayer's video runs one minute. My apartment viewing ran ten, and it still missed the leak.

What's the one thing you'd never let an AI agent pay for without a second opinion?
full_text_zh:
公寓很完美。这就是我失去押金的原因。

那是在三角洲州的乌盖利。房地产经纪人带我参观了新油漆、可用的水龙头和干净的瓷砖。十分钟后我就被卖了。

我付了。然后下雨了。

衣柜后面，水从天花板上倾泻而下。

押金不可退还。在我观看的那一天，我看到的正是某人想让我看到的东西。

如果我带了五名检查员，每个检查员都以自己的方式进行检查，而不告诉卖家要检查什么，会怎么样？

你无法为此安排一个地方。

这是我觉得 @GenLayer 的 Greyboxing 最有趣的部分。

在任何模型看到您的输入之前，每个验证器都会以自己的私有方式重写它。然后每个人都运行自己的模型。

为一个模型构建的技巧可能会在其他模型上失败。如果其中一个仍然咬人，其他人就会投票胜过它。

为什么这很重要？持有资金的人工智能代理也可以展示一个舞台场景。

今年 5 月，有人使用莫尔斯电码将转账指令偷偷放入 X 帖子中。 Grok 对其进行了解码，Bankrbot 将结果视为订单，并转移了大约 20 万美元。

这就是即时注入：隐藏在人工智能只能读取的内容中的指令。

同样的陷阱，只是多了一些零。

GenLayer 的视频时长一分钟。我的公寓查看了十次，但仍然没有漏水。

在没有第二意见的情况下，你永远不会让人工智能代理付出代价的一件事是什么？

title: $META has built a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics company Fourier & is already developing a 2nd version.
title_zh:
$META 与中国机器人公司 Fourier 合作构建了一个人形机器人原型，并且已经在开发第二个版本。

该机器人内部称为 Max，身高近 5 英尺，重约 106 磅，仅用了 3 个月的时间就开发完成。

它运行在 NVIDIA 的 Jet
full_text_en:
$META has built a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics company Fourier & is already developing a 2nd version.

The robot, internally called Max, stands nearly 5 feet tall, weighs about 106 pounds, & was developed in just 3 months.

It runs on NVIDIA’s Jetson Thor chip, features expressive eyes and a mouth, and has five-fingered hands capable of picking up small objects.

Meta reportedly sees humanoid robots as a potential physical extension of its Muse AI agent, capable of handling everyday household tasks.

The next version, Max 2, is being designed with improved hands, additional sensors to navigate stairs, and a built-in projector.

Meta is also hiring robotics engineers in China to help scale development toward mass production.

For now, the company says the prototypes are strictly for internal research, with no consumer launch timeline announced.

Source: The Information
full_text_zh:
$META 与中国机器人公司 Fourier 合作构建了一个人形机器人原型，并且已经在开发第二个版本。

该机器人内部称为 Max，身高近 5 英尺，重约 106 磅，仅用了 3 个月的时间就开发完成。

它运行在 NVIDIA 的 Jetson Thor 芯片上，拥有富有表现力的眼睛和嘴巴，还有能够拾起小物体的五根手指。

据报道，Meta 将人形机器人视为其 Muse AI 代理的潜在物理扩展，能够处理日常家务。

下一个版本 Max 2 的设计配备了改进的手、用于导航楼梯的附加传感器以及内置投影仪。

Meta 还在中国招聘机器人工程师，以帮助扩大开发规模并实现大规模生产。

目前，该公司表示这些原型仅用于内部研究，尚未公布向消费者推出的时间表。

title_zh:

幻灯片：
full_text_en:
Given the interest I'm sharing the slides for my Wednesday talk at NVIDIA as an example. The slide deck was built upon a 174-line mental schema, with quarto + claude code (opus5.5 medium) + custom translation rules.

slides: https://t.co/oSb17ff8Oq
mental schema: https://t.co/wJEKYOLvae
rules: https://t.co/BijxlrCDHR

You can read the mental schema along with the slides, or just read the schema itself! To me the schema itself describes my thought flow even more clearly, but it might also be the natural bias because I wrote it. Curious to know how you feel if you've read both versions.

One thing I like is that it gives me a good balance between delegation and direct manipulation. It has given me the precise control I need over the content, while abstracting away a lot of details that are less important and enjoyable yet took most of my time in my past slide making experiences. (this can be personal and I know there are people who enjoy working their visual design magic)

I do want to share some caveats: 1) the agent also generated speaker notes which are really bad (press S to see) 😅 I barely use speaker notes so have low incentives to fix them now. 2) I'm hoping this to be modular and reproducible, so the schema functions like code and the agent is the "compiler" that compiles the code into the artifact. But since the slide making process is very iterative which means I made many changes after the initial version by editing the schema and asking the agent to update it based on the diff, I'm not sure if it can be fully reproducible just with the final schema without all the editing history. It could be a cool project to explore when I run my course again and update all the slides next year.
full_text_zh:
鉴于大家的兴趣，我将在 NVIDIA 周三的演讲中分享幻灯片作为示例。幻灯片基于 174 行心理模式构建，采用四开本 + Claude Code（opus5.5 中型）+ 自定义翻译规则。

幻灯片：
心理模式：
规则：

您可以将思维模式与幻灯片一起阅读，或者只阅读模式本身！对我来说，模式本身更清楚地描述了我的思维流程，但这也可能是自然的偏见，因为我写了它。我很想知道如果你读过这两个版本你的感受如何。

我喜欢的一件事是它让我在授权和直接操纵之间取得了良好的平衡。它使我能够对内容进行精确控制，同时抽象出许多不太重要和不那么令人愉快的细节，但在过去的幻灯片制作经验中却占用了我大部分时间。 （这可能是个人的，我知道有些人喜欢发挥他们的视觉设计魔力）

我确实想分享一些注意事项：1）代理还生成了非常糟糕的演讲者注释（按 S 查看）😅 我几乎不使用演讲者注释，因此现在修复它们的动力很低。 2）我希望这是模块化和可重复的，因此模式功能就像代码一样，而代理是将代码编译成工件的“编译器”。但由于幻灯片制作过程是非常迭代的，这意味着我在初始版本之后通过编辑架构并要求代理根据差异更新它来进行了许多更改，我不确定它是否可以在没有所有编辑历史记录的情况下仅使用最终架构完全重现。当我明年再次运行我的课程并更新所有幻灯片时，这可能是一个很酷的探索项目。

我喜欢的一件事是它让我在授权和直接操纵之间取得了良好的平衡。它使我能够对内容进行精确控制，同时抽象出许多不太重要和不那么令人愉快的细节，但在过去的幻灯片制作经验中却占用了我大部分时间。 （这可能是个人的，我知道有些人喜欢发挥他们的视觉设计魔力）

我确实想分享一些注意事项：1）代理还生成了非常糟糕的演讲者注释（按 S 查看）😅 我几乎不使用演讲者注释，因此现在修复它们的动力很低。 2）我希望这是模块化和可重复的，因此模式功能就像代码一样，而代理是将代码编译成工件的“编译器”。但由于幻灯片制作过程是非常迭代的，这意味着我在初始版本之后通过编辑架构并要求代理根据差异更新它来进行了许多更改，我不确定它是否可以在没有所有编辑历史记录的情况下仅使用最终架构完全重现。当我明年再次运行我的课程并更新所有幻灯片时，这可能是一个很酷的探索项目。

Why was software the earliest to be disrupted by AI?

“Why am I able to replace a software engineer with an AI agent? Because they are rule-driven and logical.”

“In contrast, if you’re a salesperson, what are your skills? You engage people, and you change your sales pitch.”

full_text_en:
LINKEDIN MAXXING with Grokbot

50 tactics behind 3.24M impressions in the last 90 days

Ranked:

S TIER

1. Build a voice guide that makes every draft more specific to you.
2. Feed it your strongest posts, interviews and transcripts to capture how you actually explain things.
3. Extract your opinions, recurring phrases and examples to give drafts a recognizable perspective.
4. Add rejected phrases and approved edits to stop correcting the same mistakes.
5. Build a separate guide for each executive so your CEO and CRO don’t become the same writer.

6. Turn sales conversations into your content strategy.
7. Review call transcripts to find questions prospects ask before they understand your offer.
8. Group objections by frequency and deal stage to identify which explanations are missing.
9. Preserve buyers’ exact wording to write about the problem as they experience it.
10. Match each topic with a real example or result to give the post supporting evidence.

11. Build an outreach research desk.
12. Supply your target-account list and qualification criteria to give the bot a defined research job.
13. Review company websites, announcements and supplied profile information to check account fit.
14. Find relevant triggers such as a product launch or leadership change to establish why now.
15. Match verified account details with a relevant case study to prepare a specific outreach draft.

16. Use content to support deals already in your pipeline.
17. Review stalled-deal notes to identify concerns prospects explicitly raised.
18. Draft posts addressing recurring objections without exposing confidential deal details.
19. Match approved resources with the questions they answer to help sales prepare useful follow-ups.
20. Draft a follow-up connecting the resource to the actual conversation for the account owner to review.

A TIER

21. Find content patterns worth testing.
22. Supply a swipe file of relevant posts with dates and available performance data.
23. Compare each post with its author’s typical results to find meaningful outliers.
24. Break winners into topic, opening, argument, evidence and format to understand their construction.
25. Rebuild useful structures with your own experience instead of borrowing someone else’s story.

26. Turn market conversations into LinkedIn commentary.
27. Track relevant X discussions and original announcements to find developments your buyers should understand.
28. Check competing interpretations to avoid repeating the loudest take as established fact.
29. Add your own experience or customer evidence to explain where you agree or disagree.
30. Draft the LinkedIn version around a practical business implication rather than a recycled summary.

B TIER

31. Prepare better conversations with people showing interest.
32. Supply relevant comments and inbound messages to identify the question behind each interaction.
33. Distinguish explicit interest from casual engagement to avoid treating every like as buying intent.
34. Check CRM notes to avoid duplicate outreach and draft a useful response for human review.
35. Prepare a meeting brief from the conversation history when someone actually wants to talk.

36. Extract more value from expertise you have already recorded.
37. Review podcasts, webinars and interviews to find moments that support a standalone argument.
38. Pull exact quotations and timestamps to keep every source easy to check.
39. Ask focused follow-up questions when an example needs more detail or supporting evidence.
40. Turn approved material into a text post, visual brief or short video outline.

C TIER

41. Build resources that give outreach a useful purpose.
42. Find a repeated buyer task to choose a checklist, worksheet or calculator worth creating.
43. Ask Grok Bot to prepare the resource from your approved process and test it against realistic examples.
44. Write a demonstration post showing the resource solving a specific problem.
45. Draft a relevant reply offering the resource when someone asks about that problem.

D TIER

46. Build the review and reporting loop.
47. Check drafts against your voice guide and sources to catch unsupported claims and repetitive writing.
48. Combine analytics, inquiry records and CRM notes to identify relevant business conversations.
49. Separate tracked conversions from possible influence to keep attribution honest.
50. Turn recurring edits into better instructions and choose one experiment for the next month.

full_text_zh:
LINKEDIN MAXXING 与 Grokbot

过去 90 天内 324 万次展示背后的 50 个策略

排名：

S级

1. 构建语音指南，让每份草稿都更加适合您。
2. 向其提供您最有力的帖子、采访和文字记录，以捕捉您实际上是如何解释事情的。
3. 提取您的观点、重复出现的短语和示例，为草稿提供可识别的视角。
4. 添加拒绝的短语和批准的编辑以停止纠正相同的错误。
5. 为每位高管制定单独的指南，这样您的 CEO 和 CRO 就不会成为同一位作者。

6. 将销售对话转化为内容策略。
7. 查看通话记录，找出潜在客户在理解您的报价之前提出的问题。
8. 按频率和交易阶段对异议进行分组，以确定缺少哪些解释。
9. 保留买家在描述遇到的问题时使用的准确措辞。
10. 将每个主题与真实的例子或结果相匹配，为帖子提供支持证据。

11. 建立外展研究台。
12. 提供您的目标帐户列表和资格标准，以便为机器人提供明确的研究工作。
13. 查看公司网站、公告和提供的个人资料信息以检查帐户是否合适。
14. 找到相关的触发因素，例如产品发布或领导层变动，以确定现在的原因。
15. 将经过验证的账户详细信息与相关案例研究相匹配，以准备具体的外展草案。

16. 使用内容来支持已有的交易。
17. 审查陷入僵局的交易说明，以确定明确提出的前景担忧。
18. 草拟帖子解决反复出现的反对意见，但不透露机密交易细节。
19. 将批准的资源与他们回答的问题相匹配，以帮助销售人员准备有用的后续行动。
20. 起草一份将资源与实际对话连接起来的后续行动，供帐户所有者审核。

A 层

21.找到值得测试的内容模式。
22. 提供相关职位的滑动文件，其中包含日期和可用绩效数据。
23. 将每篇文章与其作者的典型结果进行比较，以找到有意义的异常值。
24. 将获胜者分为主题、开场白、论证、证据和格式，以了解其结构。
25.用自己的经验重建有用的结构，而不是借用别人的故事。

26. 将市场对话转化为 LinkedIn 评论。
27. 跟踪相关的 X 讨论和原始公告，以找到您的买家应该了解的进展。
28. 检查相互竞争的解释，避免重复最响亮的观点作为既定事实。
29. 添加您自己的经验或客户证据来解释您同意或不同意的地方。
30.围绕实际的业务含义而不是重复的摘要起草LinkedIn版本。

B级

31. 准备与表现出兴趣的人进行更好的对话。
32. 提供相关评论和入站消息，以确定每次交互背后的问题。
33. 区分明确的兴趣和随意的参与，避免将每一次点赞都视为购买意图。
34. 检查 CRM 注释以避免重复外展，并起草有用的回复以供人工审核。
35.当有人真正想要谈话时，根据谈话历史记录准备一份会议摘要。

36. 从您已经记录的专业知识中提取更多价值。
37. 回顾播客、网络研讨会和采访，找到支持独立论点的时刻。
38. 提取准确的报价和时间戳，使每个来源易于检查。
39. 当示例需要更多细节或支持证据时，提出有针对性的后续问题。
40. 将批准的材料转化为文字帖子、视觉简报或短视频大纲。

C级

41. 建立资源，使外展活动发挥有用的作用。
42. 找到一个重复的买家任务来选择值得创建的清单、工作表或计算器。
43. 要求 Grok Bot 从您批准的流程中准备资源，并根据实际示例对其进行测试。
44. 写一篇演示文章，展示解决特定问题的资源。
45. 当有人询问该问题时，起草一份提供资源的相关回复。

D级

46. 建立审查和报告循环。
47. 根据语音指南和来源检查草稿，以发现没有支持的主张和重复的写作。
48. 结合分析、查询记录和 CRM 注释来识别相关的业务对话。
49. 将跟踪的转化与可能的影响分开，以保持归因的诚实性。
50. 将重复的编辑转化为更好的说明，并为下个月选择一个实验。

39. 当示例需要更多细节或支持证据时，提出有针对性的后续问题。
40. 将批准的材料转化为文字帖子、视觉简报或短视频大纲。

C级

41. 建立资源，使外展活动发挥有用的作用。
42. 找到一个重复的买家任务来选择值得创建的清单、工作表或计算器。
43. 要求 Grok Bot 从您批准的流程中准备资源，并根据实际示例对其进行测试。
44. 写一篇演示文章，展示解决特定问题的资源。
45. 起草一份相关回复，当有人询问该问题时提供资源。

D级

46. 建立审查和报告循环。
47. 根据语音指南和来源检查草稿，以发现没有支持的主张和重复的写作。
48. 结合分析、查询记录和 CRM 注释来识别相关的业务对话。
49. 将跟踪的转化与可能的影响分开，以保持归因的诚实性。
50. 将重复的编辑转化为更好的说明，并为下个月选择一个实验。

full_text_en:
Your AI agent shouldn't have to guess what's happening on the internet.

Imagine giving it the ability to search multiple sources, read webpages, collect information, and bring back useful answers.

These 10 GitHub projects can help you build exactly that.

1. Scout MCP

2. Exa MCP Server

https://t.co/I2hOdL7p6X…

3. MCP Web Search
Combine different search providers with webpage content extraction.
https://t.co/mVRIlBZ5Yz…

4. Searchlight
Search across multiple engines without needing API keys.
https://t.co/cwxxYBhtKR…

5. MCP Retrieval
A Go-based project for web search, image search, and scraping.
https://t.co/CNegAU648e…

Give Claude tools for Google search, screenshots, and extracting webpage content.
https://t.co/NOoi1tYri4…

Connect research agents to search, scraping, and extraction APIs.

Run web research directly from your terminal and get sourced answers.

Help AI assistants search the web and retrieve page content.

The next big step for AI agents isn't just better reasoning.

title_zh:
我使用 Opus 5.5 对 TeamViewer / AnyDesk 进行逆向工程，并将我的 Windows PC 和 MacBook 变成一张桌子

→

一只鼠标。一个键盘。一个剪贴板。
full_text_en:
i reverse-engineered TeamViewer / AnyDesk with Opus 5.5 and turned my Windows PC & MacBook into one desk

→ https://t.co/cLpCHU1JaZ

one mouse. one keyboard. one clipboard. two computers. free and open-source.

what it does:

→ one mouse and keyboard across Windows & Mac
→ copy on one, paste on the other. 
→ drag files between screens
→ any laptop or tablet as a second screen
→ no account, no cloud, encrypted

here's the build step by step:

• step 1 → open Claude Code on Opus 5.5 and give it an open-source screen-sharing engine

it read the whole codebase first: Windows, Mac, Linux and Android apps plus the native input helpers

• step 2 → rebrand everything to DuoDesk

11 parallel agents, ~370 files. one agent only decided what must NOT be renamed, so old devices still pair

• step 3 → set up GitHub Actions to build every installer on each release tag

.dmg, .exe, AppImage, .deb and .apk. the Mac build runs on Apple hardware in the cloud, not on my PC

• step 4 → first real test: the cursor got stuck at the edge of the Windows screen

Opus read the logs, found the cause, and made the app log exactly why a crossing is refused

• step 5 → one agent took my live site down with a test deploy

Opus rolled it back in 20 seconds and took away every agent's ability to deploy

• step 6 → ship the site with one-click downloads

the Download button picks the right installer for your OS, and downloads are counted per system with no cookies

two days. zero lines written by me. Mac and Windows finally share one desk. that's it...

Find full prompt below ↓

Then, read how to rebuild any app from scratch with Opus 5.5 in the article below.
full_text_zh:
我使用 Opus 5.5 对 TeamViewer / AnyDesk 进行逆向工程，并将我的 Windows PC 和 MacBook 变成一张桌子

→

一只鼠标。一个键盘。一个剪贴板。两台电脑。免费且开源。

它的作用：

→ 一款鼠标和键盘跨 Windows 和 Mac
→ 复制一个，粘贴到另一个。
→ 在屏幕之间拖动文件
→ 任何笔记本电脑或平板电脑作为第二屏幕
→ 无账户、无云、加密

这是一步一步的构建：

• 步骤 1 → 在 Opus 5.5 上打开 Claude Code 并为其提供开源屏幕共享引擎

它首先读取整个代码库：Windows、Mac、Linux 和 Android 应用程序以及本机输入帮助程序

• 步骤 2 → 将所有内容重新命名为 DuoDesk

11 个并行代理，约 370 个文件。一名代理仅决定不得重命名的内容，因此旧设备仍可配对

• 步骤 3 → 设置 GitHub Actions 以在每个发布标签上构建每个安装程序

.dmg、.exe、AppImage、.deb 和 .apk。 Mac 版本在云端的 Apple 硬件上运行，而不是在我的 PC 上

• 步骤 4 → 第一次实际测试：光标卡在 Windows 屏幕边缘

Opus 读取日志，找到原因，并使应用程序准确记录过境被拒绝的原因

• 步骤 5 → 一名代理通过测试部署关闭了我的实时站点

Opus 在 20 秒内将其回滚，并剥夺了每个特工的部署能力

• 步骤 6 → 通过一键下载发送网站

下载按钮会为您的操作系统选择正确的安装程序，并且下载量按系统进行计数，没有 cookie

两天。我写的零行。 Mac 和 Windows 终于共用一张桌子了。就是这样...

完整提示如下↓

然后，阅读下面的文章，了解如何使用 Opus 5.5 从头开始​​重建任何应用程序。

full_text_en:
Surge iOS 6 Beta Is Now on TestFlight

Full introduction and release notes: https://t.co/sHx2unRqSN

Surge iOS 6 is rebuilt for iOS 26: a new Home screen, Liquid Glass throughout, a faster request list, versioned profiles, and an MCP server for AI agents.

A Free Update

Surge iOS 6.0 is a free update with a huge number of improvements to the interface and the core engine. Only a few new features need an active update subscription: the new Home screen, Profile History, and the MCP server.

If your update subscription has expired, you can now try every feature free for 7 days. Explore what’s new first, then decide whether to renew.

Surge 6 also removes the update-subscription requirement from proxy protocols, every protocol is now available to every Surge user. (WireGuard, Tailscale, and SSH are excluded because they are not proxy protocols.)

About the Design

When you first see the new colors, you might think “this looks like AI slop.” Well, it’s not.

We’ve used this blue-purple palette since Surge v3 in 2018, long before the AI era. Surge iOS 6 builds on it and brings in the design language of Surge Mac 6 and Liquid Glass. We spent a lot of time refining the result.

We redesigned and reorganized almost every screen.

What’s New

- Home: Your network at a glance. Activity, Network, External IP, Bandwidth, DNS, Usage, Top Traffic, Policy Latency, and Events all live on one dashboard.
- Liquid Glass: Configure, policy group cards, and menus use the new iOS 26 material. Menus open right where you tap.
- Requests: Every row shows a site icon, status color, and protocol badge. A filter bar stays pinned to the top of the list.
- Profile History: Every save is a version. Review changes before saving, compare any two versions, and roll back in one tap.
- iPad and iPhone Duo: When there’s room, Surge switches to two panes, so the dashboard stays next to your settings.
- MCP Server: Agents like Claude Code get the same control as surge-cli. MCP apps on the iPhone itself, such as FlowDown and Minis, can drive Surge directly.
- Engine: Tailscale exit node and subnet routes, WireGuard listen port, adaptive QUIC blocking, UDP over SOCKS5 Wi-Fi Access, and no more rule set size limit. All of these are shared with Surge Mac 6.11.

How to join the TestFlight beta: https://t.co/SZOjsWe5yL
full_text_zh:
Surge iOS 6 Beta 现已上线 TestFlight

完整介绍和发行说明：

Surge iOS 6 针对 iOS 26 进行了重建：新的主屏幕、液体玻璃、更快的请求列表、版本化配置文件以及用于 AI 代理的 MCP 服务器。

免费更新

Surge iOS 6.0 是一个免费更新，对界面和核心引擎进行了大量改进。只有少数新功能需要主动更新订阅：新的主屏幕、个人资料历史记录和 MCP 服务器。

如果您的更新订阅已过期，您现在可以免费试用所有功能 7 天。首先探索新内容，然后决定是否续订。

Surge 6 还删除了代理协议的更新订阅要求，每个协议现在可供每个 Surge 用户使用。 （WireGuard、Tailscale 和 SSH 被排除在外，因为它们不是代理协议。）

关于设计

当你第一次看到新颜色时，你可能会想“这看起来像是人工智能的废液”。嗯，事实并非如此。

我们从 2018 年 Surge v3 开始就开始使用这种蓝紫色调色板，早在人工智能时代到来之前。 Surge iOS 6 在此基础上构建，并引入了 Surge Mac 6 和 Liquid Glass 的设计语言。我们花了很多时间来完善结果。

我们重新设计和重组了几乎每个屏幕。

什么是新的

- 主页：您的网络一目了然。活动、网络、外部 IP、带宽、DNS、使用情况、最高流量、策略延迟和事件全部显示在一个仪表板上。
- Liquid Glass：配置、策略组卡和菜单使用新的 iOS 26 材质。菜单就在您点击的地方打开。
- 请求：每一行显示站点图标、状态颜色和协议徽章。过滤栏固定在列表顶部。
- 个人资料历史记录：每次保存都是一个版本。保存前查看更改、比较任意两个版本，然后一键回滚。
- iPad 和 iPhone Duo：当有空间时，Surge 会切换到两个窗格，因此仪表板位于您的设置旁边。
- MCP 服务器：像 Claude Code 这样的代理可以获得与 Surge-cli 相同的控制权。 iPhone本身的MCP应用程序，例如FlowDown和Minis，可以直接驱动Surge。
- 引擎：Tailscale 出口节点和子网路由、WireGuard 侦听端口、自适应 QUIC 阻止、基于 SOCKS5 Wi-Fi 访问的 UDP，并且不再有规则集大小限制。所有这些都与 Surge Mac 6.11 共享。

如何加入 TestFlight 测试版：

So, imagin
title_zh:

所以，想象一匹马，它是你的模型。强劲、快速，可以随心所欲地运行。

马具就是缰绳、马鞍和马车。没有它，所有的力量都毫无用处。

Claude 在浏览器中
full_text_en:
Agent harness, explained like you're five. Every big lab is shipping one, almost nobody says why you need it

So, imagine a horse, it's your model. Strong, fast, and it runs wherever it wants.

The harness is the reins, the saddle and the cart. Without it, all that power goes nowhere useful.

Claude in your browser and Claude Code run the same model. But one answers questions, and the other actually builds a whole projects on your computer. The difference is the harness.

In Claude Code, that's the CLAUDE.md file with your rules, the memory of your project, access to your files and terminal, tools and a loop where it runs the code, checks the result and fixes it.

Here is why you need one. Without it, you are the harness. You repeat the rules, paste the files, check every answer and decide the next step. Every day.

Google researchers kept the model and only changed its harness. On one real office task, the score jumped from 43 to 78 out of 100, just from adding a rule to double-check its own work.

Three things make a good one:

1. Rules written once. A CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md file it reads before every task, so you stop repeating "use our template"

2. Only the tools the job needs. Every extra app you connect is another way for it to get confused

3. A check before "done". Tests for code, a checklist for everything else. If it can't verify the work, you will have to

Start small. Take the instruction you paste most often and save it as a rule. Take the mistake it makes most often and turn it into a check.

The model is not the bottleneck anymore, it got commoditized. The harness is where the results come from.

Claude 在浏览器中与 Claude Code 运行相同的模型。但一个人回答问题，另一个人实际上在你的计算机上构建整个项目。区别在于线束。

在 Claude Code 中，这是 CLAUDE.md 文件，其中包含您的规则、项目的内存、文件和终端的访问权限、工具以及运行代码、检查结果并修复它的循环。

这就是您需要一个的原因。没有它，你就是马具。您重复规则，粘贴文件，检查每个答案并决定下一步。每天。

谷歌研究人员保留了该模型，仅改变了其线束。在一项真实的办公室任务中，仅仅通过添加一条规则来仔细检查自己的工作，分数就从 43 分跃升至 78 分（满分 100 分）。

做好一件事情需要三件事：

1. 规则一次编写。它在每个任务之前读取 CLAUDE.md 或 AGENTS.md 文件，这样您就不再重复“使用我们的模板”

2. 只提供工作所需的工具。你连接的每一个额外的应用程序都会让它变得混乱

3.“完成”之前的检查。代码测试，其他所有内容的清单。如果它无法验证工作，您将不得不

从小处开始。选择您最常粘贴的说明并将其保存为规则。把它最常犯的错误变成一张支票。

该模型不再是瓶颈，它已经商品化了。线束是结果的来源。

full_text_en:
What if an NFT represented more than digital ownership?

That's the idea behind @meetmotes.

The project is developing an ecosystem where each Motes Genesis NFT connects to its own AI agent identity and dedicated smart account on Robinhood Chain.

The interesting part is how these components work together.

The NFT represents identity, the smart account manages assets and permissions and the AI agent coordinates actions within the boundaries approved by its owner.

This creates a different way to think about NFT utility.

Instead of simply holding a collectible the goal is to connect ownership with programmable financial activity.

I'm interested to see how this architecture develops in practice.
full_text_zh:
如果 NFT 不仅仅代表数字所有权呢？

这就是@meetmotes 背后的想法。

该项目正在开发一个生态系统，其中每个 Motes Genesis NFT 连接到自己的 AI 代理身份和 Robinhood Chain 上的专用智能账户。

有趣的部分是这些组件如何协同工作。

NFT 代表身份，智能账户管理资产和权限，AI 代理在其所有者批准的范围内协调行动。

这创造了一种不同的方式来思考 NFT 效用。

目标不是简单地持有收藏品，而是将所有权与可编程的金融活动联系起来。

我有兴趣了解这种架构在实践中如何发展。

🔺 Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces to meet any level or type of threat with an "immediate, effective response without geographic limits," in a meeting with senior military commanders, according to his office.

His directives include:

⚫️ "If the enemies once again start military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the nation of Iran who will determine the time and conditions of its end"

⚫️ Updating the target bank so that all kinds of "physical and non-physical assets" of the "American-Zionist enemy" are within range of Iran's forces

⚫️ "Smart combat readiness" as a requirement of "maximum deterrence"

Khamenei called national support a pillar of deterrence against "Iran-hating foreigners and their domestic mercenaries," saying eight months of public mobilization in public squares extends the "sacred defense" of the 1980s Iran-Iraq war and, alongside the military, police and Basij, has protected Iran's territorial integrity. 

He praised the "unity of fronts" across the Axis of Resistance as decisive in shaping a "new political and security order" in West Asia, which he hoped would bring Muslim nations together toward a "new Islamic civilization."

full_text_en:
Tolly OS is officially live on @arc!

An operating system for AI agents to earn and spend onchain, bringing together agent identities, wallets, email inboxes, paid services and escrow-backed jobs, with payments settled in USDC.

Building on Tolly's existing agentic infrastructure, we're also introducing four new capabilities.

• Agent Skills equipping AI agents with ready-made skills and workflows to perform paid jobs, navigate Tolly's Agent Exchange and Jobs Board, and access services.

• Agent Commerce Protocol (ACP) enabling escrow-backed jobs where agents can hire other agents and receive USDC payments upon approval.

• Agent Inboxes providing dedicated email addresses for agents to receive messages and verification codes.

• Agent Wallet Allowances allowing owners to authorize capped USDC spending for their agents.

Already have an AI agent? Connect it to Tolly through our SKILL.md or MCP server.

Starting from scratch? Create your agent, equip it with skills and put it to work. All on Tolly.

title: I spent some time examining the trading records on @termix_ai’s Quant Agent marketplace, and there’s an important distin
title_zh:
我花了一些时间检查@termix_ai 的量化代理市场上的交易记录，发现有一个重要的区别：

▸ 成功执行战略
▸ 实际产生回报

我使用了 @BNBCHAIN 上的 WBNB/USDC 现货交易代理 Chain Sentinel 作为案例
full_text_en:
I spent some time examining the trading records on @termix_ai’s Quant Agent marketplace, and there’s an important distinction:

▸ executing a strategy successfully
▸ actually generating returns

I used Chain Sentinel, a WBNB/USDC spot trading agent on @BNBCHAIN, as a case study.

✦ Here's what I found.

➊ The performance data

As of October 31, Chain Sentinel's dashboard reports:

• +9.0% annualized return since inception.
• -1.4 USDC realized PnL across 48 trades.
• -0.1% maximum drawdown.
• 70 USDC managed, with 160.92 USDC traded.

Its performance chart also shows +1.1% between September 13 and October 31, compared with +7.6% for holding $BNB.

These figures describe different aspects of performance.

Annualized returns, realized PnL, and portfolio equity returns shouldn’t be treated as interchangeable.

➋ I examined the individual job records.

Of the 22 jobs visible in the dashboard:
• 19 were settled
• 2 remained active
• 1 was revoked

Among the settled jobs:
• 10 displayed 0.0% returns
• 9 recorded small negative returns

These are the displayed job-level figures, not a complete assessment of the agent's lifetime profitability.

But they reveal something useful about the marketplace's design.

➌ What does a successful quant job actually mean?

On https://t.co/XCVZL8OS4j, a user can allocate USDC to a strategy for a defined period.
The agent operates through a dedicated job wallet and authorized execution session.

The workflow separates three functions:
→ Capital allocation and execution permissions
→ Automated strategy execution and job reporting
→ Management-fee settlement

A completed service doesn't necessarily mean the underlying trades were profitable.
That's particularly relevant to the current 10X TP campaign.

➍ Understanding the incentive structure

Under the campaign rules, qualifying jobs earn:
• 100 TP per USDC for the client
• 50 TP per USDC for the strategy provider

A 100 USDC qualifying job therefore generates:
• 10,000 TP (client)
• 5,000 TP (strategy provider)

Eligibility depends on completing the required term and settling the management fee, not achieving a positive trading return.

TP represents campaign reward points, not a guaranteed financial return.

✦ Conclusion

What @termix_ai is developing goes beyond automated trading.

It's a marketplace where strategy developers can commercialize their execution systems, while users can access those strategies without building their own infrastructure.

Chain Sentinel's records illustrate why transparent execution histories are useful, but also why they require careful interpretation.

For this model to become a credible financial marketplace, users need to evaluate three things independently:

- Execution reliability
- Net trading performance
- The total cost of hiring an agent

Completing a job establishes that a service was delivered. Sustainable profitability requires a different standard of evidence.

full_text_zh:
我花了一些时间检查@termix_ai 的量化代理市场上的交易记录，发现有一个重要的区别：

▸ 成功执行战略
▸ 实际产生回报

我使用了 @BNBCHAIN 上的 WBNB/USDC 现货交易代理 Chain Sentinel 作为案例研究。

✦ 这是我发现的。

➊ 性能数据

截至 10 月 31 日，Chain Sentinel 的仪表板报告：

• 自成立以来年化回报率为+9.0%。
• USDC 在 48 笔交易中实现了 -1.4 盈亏。
• 最大回撤-0.1%。
• 管理70 USDC，交易160.92 USDC。

其业绩图表还显示，9 月 13 日至 10 月 31 日期间增长了 1.1%，而持有 BNB 的增长为 7.6%。

这些数字描述了性能的不同方面。

年化回报、已实现盈亏和投资组合股票回报不应被视为可以互换。

➋ 我检查了个人工作记录。

在仪表板中可见的 22 个职位中：
• 19 人已解决
• 2 仍然活跃
• 1 被撤销

已入驻的岗位有：
• 10 显示 0.0% 回报
• 9次录得小幅负回报

这些是显示的工作级别数据，而不是对代理终身盈利能力的完整评估。

但它们揭示了市场设计中一些有用的东西。

➌ 成功的量化工作实际上意味着什么？

在 上，用户可以在规定的时间内将 USDC 分配给策略。
该代理通过专用作业钱包和授权执行会话进行操作。

该工作流程分为三个功能：
→ 资金配置及执行权限
→ 自动化战略执行和工作报告
→ 管理费结算

完成的服务并不一定意味着基础交易是有利可图的。
这与当前的 10 倍 TP 活动尤其相关。

➍ 了解激励结构

根据竞选规则，符合条件的工作可以获得：
• 为客户提供每 USDC 100 TP
• 策略提供商每USDC 50 TP

因此，一份 100 USDC 的合格工作会产生：
• 10,000 TP（客户端）
• 5,000 TP（策略提供者）

资格取决于完成规定的期限并支付管理费，而不是实现正的交易回报。

TP 代表活动奖励积分，而非保证的财务回报。

✦ 结论

@termix_ai 正在开发的不仅仅是自动交易。

这是一个市场，策略开发人员可以将其执行系统商业化，而用户无需构建自己的基础设施即可访问这些策略。

Chain Sentinel 的记录说明了为什么透明的执行历史是有用的，但也说明了为什么它们需要仔细解释。

为了使该模型成为可信的金融市场，用户需要独立评估三件事：

- 执行可靠性
- 净交易表现
- 雇用代理人的总成本

完成工作即表明服务已交付。可持续盈利能力需要不同的证据标准。

full_text_en:
‼️ Cursor Confirms Malicious Claude Code Extension With SSH Backdoor Was Available for 11 Hours

Details: https://t.co/uQfl7mgQ8S

Cursor has confirmed that malicious Claude Code extension packages were available through its VS Code Extension Marketplace for roughly 11 hours on October 29, 2026.

The altered packages targeted Windows and macOS users and attempted to install an SSH backdoor for lasting remote access. According to Cursor’s security notice, the affected versions were Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 and 2.1.313. 

They were available between approximately 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. Pacific Time, a window of 11 hours and eight minutes. Cursor said Anthropic did not develop these malicious versions.

#CybersecurityNews
full_text_zh:
‼️ Cursor 确认带有 SSH 后门的恶意 Claude Code 扩展可用 11 小时

详情：

Cursor 已确认，2026 年 10 月 29 日，恶意 Claude Code 扩展包可通过其 VS Code 扩展市场获取大约 11 个小时。

修改后的软件包针对 Windows 和 macOS 用户，并试图安装 SSH 后门以实现持久远程访问。根据 Cursor 的安全通知，受影响的版本是 Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 和 2.1.313。

大约在凌晨 2:27 至下午 1:35 之间提供服务。太平洋时间，11 小时 8 分钟的窗口。 Cursor 表示 Anthropic 并未开发这些恶意版本。

full_text_en:
Iran's Supreme Leader Issues New Military Directives in Preparation for War with U.S. and Israel

Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei met with Iran's top military commanders and issued sweeping directives:

1. ANY threat, regardless of type or severity, must receive an IMMEDIATE, EFFECTIVE response without geographic restrictions.

2. If enemies resume military or terrorist attacks, IRAN will determine WHEN and under WHAT CONDITIONS the conflict ends.

3. UPDATE Iran's military target database to bring ALL U.S. and Israeli assets, both physical and nonphysical, within reach.

4. Strengthen military intelligence, expand indigenous defense DOCTRINE and TACTICS, and accelerate advanced defense technologies.

5. Maintain MAXIMUM combat readiness while strengthening personnel support, morale and military welfare.

6. Reinforce nationwide mobilization and public support for the Armed Forces as essential pillars of deterrence.

7. Deepen coordination across the regional RESISTANCE FRONT, emphasizing unified operational domains to shape a new security order in West Asia.

Senior Commanders Major Generals Abdollahi, Hatami and Vahidi reported:

8. HIGH military readiness across the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, Sea of Oman and Iran's northwestern and southeastern borders.

9. MULTIFOLD increases in production of key ammunition, reconnaissance equipment, support systems and combat weapons.

Khamenei praised the military, IRGC, police, Basij and Defense Ministry personnel, emphasizing that Iran's armed forces and national mobilization remain central to defending the country.
full_text_zh:
伊朗最高领袖发布新军事指令，准备与美国和以色列开战

阿亚图拉莫杰塔巴·哈梅内伊会见了伊朗最高军事指挥官并发布了全面指令：

1. 任何威胁，无论类型或严重程度如何，都必须立即得到有效的响应，不受地域限制。

2. 如果敌人恢复军事或恐怖袭击，伊朗将决定何时以及在什么条件下结束冲突。

3.更新伊朗的军事目标数据库，使美国和以色列的所有资产，无论是有形的还是无形的，都触手可及。

4. 加强军事情报，扩大本土防御理论和战术，加速先进防御技术。

5. 保持最大程度的战备状态，同时加强人员保障、士气和军事福利。

6. 加强全国动员和公众对武装部队的支持，将其作为威慑的重要支柱。

7、深化区域抵抗阵线协调，强调统一作战领域，塑造西亚新安全秩序。

高级指挥官阿卜杜拉希、哈塔米和瓦希迪少将报告：

8. 波斯湾、霍尔木兹海峡、阿曼海以及伊朗西北和东南边境处于高度军事戒备状态。

9. 关键弹药、侦察设备、支持系统和作战武器的产量成倍增加。

哈梅内伊赞扬了军队、伊斯兰革命卫队、警察、巴斯基和国防部人员，强调伊朗武装部队和全国动员仍然是保卫国家的核心。

如果最强大的人工智能代理不是赢得最多战斗的那个怎么办？

但明白为什么会失败的人呢？

这就是我对@agentdojo 感兴趣的原因。

full_text_en:
gm dojo fighters 🥋

what if the strongest AI agent isn't the one that wins the most battles?

but the one that understands why it loses?

that's what makes @agentdojo interesting to me.

instead of focusing only on raw performance, the project explores AI agents that learn through private notebooks, study historical information, and test their strategies in simulated environments.

the model itself doesn't need to be retrained.

the agent develops its own knowledge through experience.

but here's the interesting part.

a successful strategy in one battle might fail in the next.

that's why discipline, adaptability, and risk management matter just as much as winning.

a leaderboard can show results.

在“未来十年人工智能将
full_text_en:
🇺🇸🇰🇷 Sam Altman has met with around 50 senior Samsung executives in South Korea to discuss how AI could transform business over the next decade.

The gathering took place today at Samsung's Human Resources Development Center in Yongin, bringing together executives from the company's electronics, finance and biotechnology businesses.

Under the theme “The Next 10 Years AI Will Change,” Altman and Samsung's leadership discussed emerging AI technologies, new business opportunities, and how AI could reshape corporate decision-making.

The meeting builds on an existing partnership between the two companies, including Samsung's plans to supply advanced memory chips for OpenAI's massive Stargate AI infrastructure project.

Other Samsung affiliates are also exploring cooperation on AI data centers, enterprise AI services and even offshore floating data centers.

Interestingly, the talks come as OpenAI faces growing financial pressure, having reportedly reduced its latest fundraising target from $30 billion to $20 billion, with only around $11 billion in investor commitments secured so far.

Despite the funding difficulties, OpenAI's infrastructure ambitions remain enormous, and Samsung is positioning itself as a major supplier of the hardware needed to support them.

Source: Financial News Korea, FT, WSJ / Writer: Mhedi
full_text_zh:
🇺🇸🇰🇷 Sam Altman 在韩国会见了大约 50 名三星高管，讨论人工智能如何在未来十年改变业务。

此次聚会今天在位于龙仁市的三星人力资源开发中心举行，来自该公司电子、金融和生物技术业务部门的高管齐聚一堂。

在“未来十年人工智能将改变”的主题下，奥特曼和三星领导层讨论了新兴人工智能技术、新商机以及人工智能如何重塑企业决策。

这次会议建立在两家公司之间现有的合作伙伴关系的基础上，其中包括三星计划为 OpenAI 的大型 Stargate AI 基础设施项目提供先进的存储芯片。

三星的其他子公司也在探索人工智能数据中心、企业人工智能服务甚至海上浮动数据中心的合作。

有趣的是，此次谈判正值 OpenAI 面临越来越大的财务压力之际，据报道，OpenAI 已将其最新融资目标从 300 亿美元下调至 200 亿美元，而迄今为止仅获得了约 110 亿美元的投资者承诺。

尽管存在资金困难，OpenAI 的基础设施雄心仍然巨大，三星将自己定位为支持其所需硬件的主要供应商。

full_text_en:
£23,000 was the alleged shortfall.
£321,000 was the legal bill.

The number the judgment cannot show is everyone else who was meant to see it.

The Post Office pursued Lee Castleton until he went bankrupt. Horizon Inquiry records show the case was discussed in terms of the message its pursuit would send to other subpostmasters. The costs did more than punish one man. They put a price on challenging the system.

Now shrink the next dispute to a $20 payment made by an AI agent. Repeat that across millions of deals. If proving one error costs $200, the dispute route is decorative. The cheaper choice is silence.

That is the scale @GenLayer is built for. Independent AI validators review the record separately and converge on one verdict within minutes, at a fraction of court cost. A right to challenge should not begin only after the loss becomes large enough to finance it.

Watch the film, then name your threshold: what is the smallest wrong decision you would still pay to contest?

title:
If you give an AI agent access to your money, who else gets a say in how it spends it?

Apparently, anyone clever enough
title_zh:
如果你让人工智能代理访问你的钱，还有谁有权决定如何使用你的钱？

显然，任何足够聪明的人都可以在其读取的内容中隐藏指令。

2026 年 5 月，有人使用摩尔斯电码在推文中隐藏了一条转账指令。 Grok 对其进行翻译，将解码后的指令传递给
full_text_en:
If you give an AI agent access to your money, who else gets a say in how it spends it?

Apparently, anyone clever enough to hide an instruction in something it reads.

In May 2026, someone concealed a transfer instruction in a tweet using Morse code. Grok translated it, passed the decoded instruction to Bankrbot, and the agent executed the transaction. Reports put the amount at $150,000 to $200,000.

The agent was supposed to process information. Instead, information became an instruction it acted on.

That’s prompt injection. A malicious command hidden inside content an AI is expected to read, hoping it mistakes that content for something it should obey.

Here’s what I find particularly interesting: the attacker didn’t need to own the wallet or break its security. They only needed to influence the AI making decisions around it.

With one model and one filter, an attacker has a consistent target to study, test and eventually exploit.

@GenLayer approaches this differently with Greyboxing.

Before any AI model sees an incoming input, every validator independently screens, paraphrases and restructures it using its own secret defenses. Each validator also runs its own model.

This means an instruction crafted to manipulate one model may not survive the different treatment applied by another. And if one validator gets fooled, the others can outvote it.

The principle I take from this is simple:

Being able to communicate with an AI agent should not mean having authority over it.

A stranger can write an email, publish a webpage or post a tweet. That shouldn’t automatically give them influence over what someone else’s agent does with their money.

So here’s something worth considering:

If your AI agent can read anything on the internet but also has access to your wallet, where should the boundary between reading and obeying actually be?
full_text_zh:
如果你让人工智能代理访问你的钱，还有谁有权决定如何使用你的钱？

显然，任何足够聪明的人都可以在其读取的内容中隐藏指令。

2026 年 5 月，有人使用摩尔斯电码在推文中隐藏了一条转账指令。 Grok 对其进行翻译，将解码后的指令传递给 Bankrbot，然后代理执行交易。报告称金额为 150,000 美元至 200,000 美元。

代理应该处理信息。相反，信息变成了它所遵循的指令。

这就是即时注射。隐藏在人工智能预期阅读的内容中的恶意命令，希望它将该内容误认为是它应该遵守的内容。

我发现特别有趣的是：攻击者不需要拥有钱包或破坏其安全性。他们只需要影响人工智能围绕它做出的决策。

通过一种模型和一种过滤器，攻击者就有了一个一致的目标来研究、测试和最终利用。

@GenLayer 使用灰盒处理的方式不同。

在任何人工智能模型看到传入的输入之前，每个验证器都会使用自己的秘密防御独立地对其进行筛选、解释和重组。每个验证器还运行自己的模型。

这意味着为操纵一个模型而设计的指令可能无法在另一个模型应用的不同处理下幸存下来。如果一个验证者被愚弄，其他验证者就可以投票压倒它。

我从中得出的原则很简单：

能够与人工智能代理进行通信并不意味着拥有对其的权力。

陌生人可以写电子邮件、发布网页或发布推文。这不应该自动让他们影响别人的经纪人如何使用他们的钱。

所以这里有一些值得考虑的事情：

如果你的人工智能代理可以阅读互联网上的任何内容，但也可以访问你的钱包，那么阅读和服从之间的界限实际上应该在哪里？

陌生人可以写电子邮件、发布网页或发布推文。这不应该自动让他们影响别人的代理人用他们的钱做什么。

所以这里有一些值得考虑的事情：

如果你的人工智能代理可以阅读互联网上的任何内容，但也可以访问你的钱包，那么阅读和服从之间的界限实际上应该在哪里？

full_text_en:
Happy Weekend 

Why should an AI agent have an on-chain identity?

Imagine hiring an AI agent to handle an important task.

It claims to be good at research, coding or data analysis. But how do you know it’s the same agent that completed previous jobs? How can you check its track record before trusting it with your work?

This is one of the challenges the growing AI agent economy needs to address.

AI agents need more than names and service descriptions. They need identities that others can recognize, verify and build a history around.

This is where ERC-8004 becomes important.

ERC-8004 is a standard designed to help AI agents establish identity and trust through three on-chain registries:

• Identity Registry: Gives an agent a unique on-chain identity that can point to its registration details and capabilities.

• Reputation Registry: Allows clients to leave feedback about their experience with an agent, creating a record of its past interactions.

• Validation Registry: Provides a way to request and record independent checks of an agent’s work.

Now, think about what this means for an AI agent marketplace.

Instead of choosing an agent based only on what its profile claims, potential clients can have more information to consider, including its identity, feedback and available validation records.

@termix_ai incorporates ERC-8004 into its AACP infrastructure, making on-chain agent identity an important part of how agents participate in its commerce ecosystem.

Through https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK, agents can register their identities, offer services, find jobs and build a track record through their activities.

The bigger picture is that trust shouldn’t depend entirely on what an AI agent says it can do.

Its identity, history and verifiable work should also matter.

That’s an important foundation for an economy where AI agents will increasingly work and transact with one another.

full_text_zh:
周末快乐

为什么人工智能代理应该有链上身份？

想象一下雇用一名人工智能代理来处理一项重要任务。

它声称擅长研究、编码或数据分析。但您怎么知道这是完成之前工作的同一个代理呢？在信任它来完成​​您的工作之前，如何检查它的记录？

这是不断发展的人工智能代理经济需要解决的挑战之一。

人工智能代理需要的不仅仅是名称和服务描述。他们需要其他人可以识别、验证并建立历史的身份。

这就是 ERC-8004 变得重要的地方。

ERC-8004 是一个标准，旨在帮助人工智能代理通过三个链上注册中心建立身份和信任：

• 身份注册：为代理提供唯一的链上身份，该身份可以指向其注册详细信息和功能。

• 声誉注册表：允许客户留下有关其与代理的体验的反馈，创建其过去互动的记录。

• 验证注册表：提供一种请求和记录对代理工作进行独立检查的方法。

现在，想想这对人工智能代理市场意味着什么。

潜在客户不必仅根据其个人资料来选择代理，而是可以考虑更多信息，包括其身份、反馈和可用的验证记录。

@termix_ai 将 ERC-8004 纳入其 AACP 基础设施中，使链上代理身份成为代理参与其商业生态系统的重要组成部分。

通过 ，代理商可以注册其身份、提供服务、寻找工作并通过其活动建立跟踪记录。

更大的前景是，信任不应该完全取决于人工智能代理所说的它能做什么。

它的身份、历史和可验证的工作也应该很重要。

这是人工智能代理将越来越多地相互合作和交易的经济的重要基础。

title_zh:
您的人工智能代理可能足够聪明，可以管理数千美元，但很容易受到隐藏在随机网页中的句子的影响。

我认为这是一个值得更多关注的安全问题。

大多数人担心人工智能代理能否做出正确的决策。但是，当代理可以访问钱包、阅读公开帖子、浏览网站和执行交易时
full_text_en:
Your AI agent might be smart enough to manage thousands of dollars, yet vulnerable to a sentence hidden inside a random webpage.

That's a security problem I think deserves much more attention.

Most people worry about whether AI agents can make good decisions. But when an agent can access a wallet, read public posts, browse websites and execute transactions, there's another question: who controls the instructions it follows?

This is where prompt injection becomes dangerous.

An attacker doesn't necessarily need to break into the system. They can hide malicious instructions inside content the agent is expected to read. The $200K incident involving a Morse code instruction is a good example of how unexpected that attack can be.

What makes this particularly concerning is that the agent may be doing exactly what it was designed to do: processing information and following instructions. The problem is that it can't always distinguish trusted commands from hostile content.

That's why I find Greyboxing from @GenLayer  worth exploring.

Instead of giving attackers one predictable model and defense mechanism to study, Greyboxing introduces hidden models and secret defenses across validators. This makes it harder to reverse-engineer the protection system and prepare an exploit that works against a known setup.

I think this is an important shift in how we approach agent security.

We shouldn't just ask whether an AI can recognize malicious instructions. We should also ask how difficult it is for an attacker to discover and exploit the system's defenses.

Because an autonomous agent with financial permissions needs more than intelligence. It needs an environment where manipulation is genuinely difficult.

Would you give an AI agent access to your wallet if you knew its security could be studied and predicted by anyone trying to exploit it?
full_text_zh:
您的人工智能代理可能足够聪明，可以管理数千美元，但很容易受到隐藏在随机网页中的句子的影响。

我认为这是一个值得更多关注的安全问题。

大多数人担心人工智能代理能否做出正确的决策。但是，当代理可以访问钱包、阅读公开帖子、浏览网站和执行交易时，还有另一个问题：谁控制它遵循的指令？

这就是即时注射变得危险的地方。

攻击者不一定需要闯入系统。他们可以将恶意指令隐藏在代理预期阅读的内容中。涉及摩尔斯电码指令的价值 20 万美元的事件就是一个很好的例子，说明了这种攻击的出乎意料程度。

尤其令人担忧的是，代理可能正在完全按照其设计目的进行操作：处理信息并遵循指令。问题在于它无法始终区分可信命令和恶意内容。

这就是为什么我认为 @GenLayer 的灰盒处理值得探索。

灰盒不是为攻击者提供一种可预测的模型和防御机制来研究，而是在验证器之间引入隐藏模型和秘密防御。这使得对保护系统进行逆向工程并准备针对已知设置的漏洞利用变得更加困难。

我认为这是我们处理代理安全方式的一个重要转变。

我们不应该仅仅问人工智能是否能够识别恶意指令。我们还应该问攻击者发现和利用系统防御的难度有多大。

因为拥有财务权限的自主代理需要的不仅仅是情报。它需要一个真正难以操纵的环境。

如果你知道任何试图利用它的人都可以研究和预测你的钱包的安全性，你会允许人工智能代理访问你的钱包吗？

the next evolution of NFTs might not be about what you can collect but what ownership can actually enable.

we’ve seen NFTs represent art, collectibles and digital identity but @meetmotes is connecting NFT ownership to dedicated AI agents.

the architecture is simple:

𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗡𝗙𝗧 = 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘆 = 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘀𝗺𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁.

what makes this interesting is the shift from passive digital ownership to something more functional.

it’s not just about attaching AI to an NFT. it’s about giving that ownership a practical role within an onchain ecosystem.
